sections.html:
Common name: Niger Oto. Type locality: Rio das Pedras of Rio Ribeira, Brazil. Size: 6 cm SL.

A non-descript species with an attractive if low key horizontally striped and mottled patterning. Lives sympatrically with Parotocinclus maculicauda.
South America: Ribeira de Iguape River basin, rivers of São Paulo State, Brazil.
Really does best in a planted aquarium, other cover is not necessary although the fish has at least a passing affinity with rounded pebbles.

These fish appear to be predominantly herbivorous and will readily feed from a wide array of aquarium fare. Algae discs can make up a good portion of their diet, supplemented with any number of additional prepared flake or pellet foods.
Peaceful. Suggested tankmates: most small community fishes that prefer a little current and temperatures on the lower side.
Females are larger, broader across the pectoral to dorsal area and slightly duller in colouration.
These fish are egg scatterers, breeding in a fashion much like a member of the callichthyid genus Corydoras.
Kosmos, Rio de Janeiro [Rev. Art. Sci. Litt.] v. 5 (no. 2) (for 1907), pp [2].
